key_insight: Shear bands formed without measurable differences in local surfactant diffusion or displacement scaling, indicating that flow-induced micellar chain scission is not a dominant mechanism in this system.
engineering_relevance: Constitutive models for these wormlike micelles should not assume that shear banding necessarily entails substantial chain scission.
method: Compare non-shear-banding (R = 0.4) and shear-banding (R = 0.53) CPyCl/NaSal/D₂O solutions.
Measure local diffusion using spatially resolved rheo-diffusion NMR and velocity-compensated diffusion measurements.
Characterize flow bands using rheo-optical imaging and velocity measurements in Taylor–Couette geometry.
evidence_signal: Within the shear-banding stress plateau, local surfactant self-diffusivity remained spatially uniform, with no measurable difference in mean-squared-displacement scaling between low- and high-shear bands.
watch_item: The conclusion is specific to the tested formulations and measurement sensitivity; unchanged diffusion does not rule out all microstructural changes.
paper_title: Probing Flow-Induced Chain Scission in Shear-Banding Wormlike Micelles
